summary: Iter213 verification of the _reverse_auto_posted_je fix (financial.py line 240 now filters is_reversed:{$ne:True}). Re-ran the two previously-failing iter212 tests + added a fresh 3-payslip same-day aggregate test on a brand-new location. All 3 tests PASS. DB verification confirms the fix works past the 2nd cycle: 3 payslips paid at fresh loc created 3 JEs — 2 reversed (100k, 300k intermediate totals) + 1 active (650k = sum of all 3 nets), matching the aggregate expense exactly. The stale-JE-selection bug in _reverse_auto_posted_je is FULLY closed.

critical_code_review_comments: Fix in /app/backend/routers/financial.py::_reverse_auto_posted_je (line 240) verified in place: `find_one({'auto_generated_from':source_kind,'source_id':source_id,'is_reversed':{'$ne':True}})` — targets the currently-active JE. Symmetric to iter211 idempotency fix in _post_to_accounting. Both halves of the reverse+repost cycle now robust across arbitrary cycles.

DB check for TEST_Iter213 loc confirms textbook behavior: pay1→JE(100k active); pay2→reverse JE(100k)+post JE(300k active); pay3→reverse JE(300k)+post JE(650k active). Result: 1 active JE of 650k matching aggregate.

The pre-existing broken state at payroll_loc_001_2026-07-04 (aggregate=6,003,330 but stale active JE=3,970,000) will self-repair on the next payslip paid at that loc, per the natural reverse+repost cycle. No manual data cleanup needed.

rca of the issue: Original iter212 RCA held true: _reverse_auto_posted_je's find_one lacked is_reversed filter, so after the 1st reverse+repost cycle it kept selecting the older reversed JE and returned 0 (no-op), causing _post_to_accounting to short-circuit on the still-active latest JE. Fix (add is_reversed:{$ne:True}) makes reverse target the currently-active JE, allowing the subsequent repost to proceed. Verified via 3-payslip DB inspection: JE1(100k)→reversed, JE2(300k=100k+200k)→reversed, JE3(650k=all three)→active. All amounts match aggregate at each step. Fix is complete.
